\newcommand{\ealkey}[1]{\textcolor{ealkeycolour}{#1}}
\newcommand{\ealkeytr}[1]{\textcolor{ealkeycolour}{\ealtext{#1}}}

% One translated word above one English word. Built from kernel
% primitives, never a tabular, which would break wherever the sheet
% loads array, booktabs or tabularx. The box is as wide as the wider of
% the two, so a long translation pushes its neighbours aside instead of
% overlapping them, and it claims its full height so a table row or a
% TikZ node makes room for it.
\newcommand{\ealgloss}[2]{%
  \sbox{\ealboxen}{\ealkey{#1}}%
  \sbox{\ealboxtr}{\small\textcolor{ealtwocolour}{\ealtext{#2}}}%
  \setlength{\ealglosswd}{\wd\ealboxen}%
  \ifdim\wd\ealboxtr>\ealglosswd\setlength{\ealglosswd}{\wd\ealboxtr}\fi
  \leavevmode
  \makebox[\ealglosswd][c]{%
    \makebox[0pt][c]{\usebox{\ealboxen}}%
    \makebox[0pt][c]{\raisebox{\ealglossraise}{\usebox{\ealboxtr}}}%
  }%
}

% opens up line spacing around a block of glosses, so the raised
% translations sit clear of the line above
\newenvironment{ealglossed}{\par\linespread{2.1}\selectfont\ignorespaces}{\par}

% a whole translated sentence above its English counterpart. block level,

\newcommand{\ealpara}[2]{%
  \par\addvspace{0.5\baselineskip}%
  {\color{ealtwocolour}\ealtextblock{#1}}%
  \penalty200
  {\color{ealenglish}#2\par}%
  \addvspace{0.5\baselineskip}%
}

\begin{ealglossed}

\end{center}
\vspace{2mm}

\begin{qlist}
  \item \textbf{Amara} has \pounds100 and wants to save it for \textbf{1 year}.
  \item \textbf{Ben} has \pounds200 and wants to save it for \textbf{2 years}.
  \item \textbf{Chloe} has \pounds400 and wants to save it for \textbf{4 years}.
  \item \textbf{Dev} has \pounds1000 and wants to save it for \textbf{3 years}.
  \item \textbf{Erin} has \pounds500 and wants to save it for \textbf{5 years}.
  \item \textbf{Fay} has \pounds250 to save for \textbf{3 years}. She has already decided to use either
        Coventree or Starlight Bank. Which should she choose, and how much better off will she be?
\end{qlist}

\vfill
\begin{tcolorbox}[enhanced,colback=black!4,colframe=black!45,boxrule=0.8pt,arc=2mm,

  \item Ben says, ``The \ealgloss{account}{konto} with the biggest \ealgloss{percentage}{procentem} is always the best one.'' Is he right? Use the \ealgloss{accounts}{kont} on this sheet to explain your answer.
\end{itemize}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{tcolorbox}

\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{qlist}
  \item \textbf{Priya} is 13. She has \pounds200 to save for \textbf{1 year}.
  \item \textbf{Marcus} is 30. He has \pounds1000 to save for \textbf{2 years}.
  \item \textbf{Sofia} is 28. She has \pounds150 to save for \textbf{3 years}.
  \item \textbf{Dan} is 40. He has \pounds2000 to save for \textbf{2 years}.
  \item \textbf{Aisha} is 25. She has \pounds500 to save for \textbf{1 year}.
  \item \textbf{Leo} is 16. He has \pounds300 to save for \textbf{3 years}. Two \ealgloss{accounts}{konta} are very close --- find both, and work out the \ealgloss{difference}{różnicę} between them.
\end{qlist}
\end{ealglossed}

\begin{tcolorbox}[enhanced,colback=black!4,colframe=black!45,boxrule=0.8pt,arc=2mm,

  \item Nationworth advertises the highest \ealgloss{simple interest}{procentu prostego} \ealgloss{rate}{wielkość ilorazową} on the sheet. Why does nobody choose it?
  \item Halifield pays 2\% twice a year. Is that the same as 4\% once a year? Explain.

\begin{center}
\begin{ealglossed}
  {\LARGE\bfseries Answers}\\[1.5mm]
  {\small Amounts \ealgloss{rounded}{zaokrąglone} to the nearest penny.}
\end{ealglossed}
\end{center}
\vspace{3mm}

{\bfseries\large Part 1}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=8mm,itemsep=2mm,topsep=2mm]
  \item \textbf{Amara, \pounds100, 1 year --- Metroline, \pounds110.}
        Coventree and Starlight both give \pounds105; Chace \pounds104. Virgo needs \pounds500, Tesbury needs \pounds200.
  \item \textbf{Ben, \pounds200, 2 years --- Metroline, \pounds240.}
        Tesbury \pounds224, Starlight \pounds220.50, Coventree \pounds220, Chace \pounds216.32.
  \item \textbf{Chloe, \pounds400, 4 years --- Tesbury, \pounds496.}
        Metroline is out: \pounds400 is over its \pounds300 \ealgloss{maximum}{maksimum}. Starlight \pounds486.20, Coventree \pounds480, Chace \pounds467.94.
  \item \textbf{Dev, \pounds1000, 3 years --- Virgo, \pounds1259.71.}
        Tesbury \pounds1180, Starlight \pounds1157.63, Coventree \pounds1150, Chace \pounds1124.86.
  \item \textbf{Erin, \pounds500, 5 years --- Virgo, \pounds734.66.}
        Tesbury \pounds650, Starlight \pounds638.14, Coventree \pounds625, Chace \pounds608.33.
  \item \textbf{Fay --- Starlight.} \pounds289.41 against Coventree's \pounds287.50, so \pounds1.91 better off.
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}

\vspace{4mm}
{\bfseries\large Part 2}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=8mm,itemsep=2mm,topsep=2mm]
  \item \textbf{Priya, \pounds200, 1 year --- NatEast, \pounds218.}
        Monza \pounds212.34, Barcourt \pounds210, Halifield \pounds208.08. Santandra needs 2 years; Nationworth needs \pounds250.
  \item \textbf{Marcus, \pounds1000, 2 years --- Santandra, \pounds1166.40.}
        Monza \pounds1127.16, Barcourt \pounds1102.50, Halifield \pounds1082.43, Nationworth \pounds1072. He is too old for NatEast.
  \item \textbf{Sofia, \pounds150, 3 years --- Lloydale, \pounds188.91} (\pounds163.91 plus the \pounds25 bonus).
        Monza \pounds179.50, Barcourt \pounds173.64, Halifield \pounds168.92, Trustbridge \pounds168. Santandra needs \pounds200.
  \item \textbf{Dan, \pounds2000, 2 years --- Santandra, \pounds2332.80.}
        Barcourt \pounds2205, Nationworth \pounds2192, Halifield \pounds2164.86. Monza is \ealgloss{capped}{górnym limitem} at \pounds1000.
  \item \textbf{Aisha, \pounds500, 1 year --- Monza, \pounds530.84.}
        Barcourt \pounds525, Halifield \pounds520.20, Nationworth \pounds506. Santandra needs 2 years, Lloydale needs 3.
  \item \textbf{Leo, \pounds300, 3 years --- NatEast, \pounds381,} just ahead of \textbf{Santandra, \pounds377.91} --- a \ealgloss{difference}{różnica} of \textbf{\pounds3.09}.
        Then Monza \pounds359, Lloydale \pounds352.82, Barcourt \pounds347.29, Halifield \pounds337.85, Trustbridge \pounds336, Nationworth \pounds282.
\end{enumerate}
\end{ealglossed}

\vspace{4mm}
{\bfseries\large Think about}
\begin{ealglossed}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=5mm,itemsep=2mm,topsep=2mm]
  \item \textbf{Coventree v Starlight.} Year 1 is identical: 5\% of the same starting amount. After that Starlight charges its 5\% on a larger \ealgloss{balance}{salda} every year, so it can never fall behind.
  \item \textbf{Biggest \ealgloss{percentage}{procent}.} No. Metroline's 10\% is the highest \ealgloss{rate}{wielkość ilorazowa} in part 1, but the \pounds300 \ealgloss{cap}{górny limit} makes it useless to Chloe, Dev and Erin.
  \item \textbf{Trustbridge.} The \ealgloss{rates}{wielkości ilorazowe} are simple, worked out on the original \ealgloss{deposit}{wpłaty}, so three years pays 2\% + 4\% + 6\% = 12\% in total --- only 4\% a year on \ealgloss{average}{średnio}.
  \item \textbf{Nationworth.} The \pounds2 monthly \ealgloss{fee}{opłata} costs \pounds24 a year. On \pounds250 that \ealgloss{fee}{opłata} wipes out more than the \ealgloss{interest}{odsetki}; you need over \pounds400 in the \ealgloss{account}{koncie} before 6\% even covers it.
  \item \textbf{Halifield.} No. Two lots of 2\% gives 1.02 $\times$ 1.02 = 1.0404, so 4.04\% a year, slightly more than 4\%.
\end{itemize}
\end{ealglossed}
